correctness.rationale: The fixed-point recurrence \(x(2a)=0\), \(x(2a+1)=x(a)+1\) establishes \(x(a)=v_2(a+1)\bmod m\). A full induction constructs \(\sigma^k(a)=U_k(a+k\bmod m)\), \(U_{k+1}=U_k(k\bmod m)U_k\). For every offset \(0\le r<2^k\), two boundary portions reconstruct U_k exactly in Parikh count; this proves the unaligned-window identity. Its invertible cyclic permutation proves the complete Abelian-power occurrence-set dilation. Base-letter alternation and the impossibility of consecutive vanishing odd positions give sharp square/cube/fourth-power cases. A summable geometric valuation law establishes densities; dyadic periodic approximants establish all finite-factor frequencies. The \(m=2\) and \(k=0\) boundaries are addressed. The packaged verification script independently reconstructed the sequence and completed 318792 exact checks for \(2\le m\le9\) and \(0\le k\le6\); these checks do not serve as infinite certification.

value.rationale: Abelian powers are a standard nontrivial invariant of infinite words; the natural family of generalized period-doubling substitutions provides structured examples beyond binary. The complete all-position/all-alphabet classification at every dyadic period and exact positive densities for squares and cubes reveal a sharp Abelian exponent boundary of three. The unaligned-window identity also reduces every arbitrary-period occurrence question to odd periods and exactly transports full Parikh-class frequency distributions. These are motivated, infinite structural classifications, not a textbook scalar count, small arbitrary cutoff, or a mere substitution of parameters. The unresolved odd-period cases are clearly excluded rather than inferred.
